idiom_name: typed placeholder plus an assertion, or an optional/defaulted parameter instead
implementation_notes: The runtime is JavaScript, where an argument could simply be omitted, but with strictNullChecks on, null and undefined are not assignable to a declared parameter type, so the placeholder needs an explicit escape at the call site: make the parameter optional or defaulted in its signature, or assert a typed placeholder ({} as Logger, undefined as unknown as Logger, null!). Prefer changing the signature over asserting, because an assertion tells the compiler nothing and a later path change fails at runtime inside the SUT; a test-local empty interface ({}) is a third option that keeps the cast short. Vitest and Jest produce recording doubles instead (vi.fn(), jest.fn()) which answer every call with undefined and record arguments - spies and stubs, not dummies - and using one as a placeholder hides the moment the parameter is read.
pitfalls: as-assertions and non-null assertions switch off checking exactly where the placeholder's validity matters, so the compiler cannot warn when the path starts reading the parameter and the failure moves into the SUT.

undefined and null behave differently for default parameters, for optional properties and for strict equality, and exactOptionalPropertyTypes changes what is assignable; passing the wrong one silently defeats defaults.

{} as Logger only type-checks while Logger has no required members; adding one turns every placeholder into a compile error (the good outcome) unless the cast goes through unknown, which suppresses exactly that signal.
